title: Rosanne Cash Postpones Trio of Shows Due to ‘Unexpected Medical Emergency’
summary: The impacted gigs were slated to take place in Montana and Wyoming.
contentText:
Rosanne Cash is postponing a trio of shows on her current U.S. tour due to what her management team said was an unspecified “ unexpected medical emergency .” According to a statement posted on the 71-year-old singer’s Instagram on Monday (Sept. 7), Cash has pushed back planned dates in Sheridan, Wyo. on Tuesday (Sept. 8), as well as Billings, Mont. on Wednesday (Sept. 9) and Bozeman, Mont. on Saturday (Sept. 12).

The statement noted that the Grammy-winning eldest daughter of late country icon Johnny Cash “is recovering under her doctors’ supervision, who have recommended a temporary restriction on travel and performing.” That restriction has resulted in the postponing of the Wyoming and Montana shows. At press time, the dates for the rescheduled gigs had not been announced yet.

Cash has one more scheduled show on her U.S. swing — a Sept.19 show at the Riceland Hall inside A-State Fowler Center in Jonesboro, Ark. — before she is slated to take a brief pause in advance of a short run of European shows slated to kick off on Oct. 15 at the Music Hall Worpswede in Worpswede, Germany. The singer’s final scheduled 2026 date is a Nov. 9 stop at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville.

Cash’s most recent release is a duet with The National singer Matt Berninger on a cover of the Velvet Underground’s “Who Loves the Sun,” released in March as the opening theme for the Will Forte/D’Arcy Carden Hulu crime comedy series Sunny Nights . She recently shared the stage with Judy Collins, Mary Chapin Carpenter, Amanda Shires and Madeleine Peyroux at the Tanglewood Music Festival on Aug. 30 as part of the special Sweet Judy Blue Eyes: Farewell Tour marking Collins’ final Tanglewood performance.
